title: Off-shell gauge complexes, BRST doublets and anomaly obstructions

items.title: Abelian local jet BRST differential
items.statement:
Use the smooth off-shell coordinate model $\mathbb M=\mathbb R^4$, with $x^0=c_{\mathrm{light}}t$ in SI coordinates, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, increasing $x^0$ as the future direction, and standard orientation. The scalar time-ordering convention sets $c_{\mathrm{light}}=1$, so $x^0$ is the length coordinate in that convention as well. Here off shell means that no field equation is imposed. Take smooth real components $a_\mu\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb R)$ and a smooth commuting matter field $\psi\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb C^4)$. Use the normalized real potential $a=a_\mu dx^\mu$ and dimensionless coupling $g=q\sqrt{\mu_0c_{\mathrm{light}}/\hbar}$ of the charged-gauge-data convention; $a_\mu$ has units $\mathrm m^{-1}$, $g$ is dimensionless, and $\psi$ has units $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$. The exact supplier convention is $a'_\mu=a_\mu+\partial_\mu\alpha$, $\psi'=e^{ig\alpha}\psi$, for a smooth dimensionless real infinitesimal gauge parameter $\alpha$.

Let $\mathcal P$ be the free graded-commutative $\mathbb C$-algebra over $C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb C)$ generated by the finite jets of $a_\mu$, $\psi$, an odd ghost $c_{\mathrm{gh}}$, an odd antighost $\bar c$, and an even auxiliary variable $B$. Every element of $\mathcal P$ is a polynomial in finitely many jet coordinates. The fields $a_\mu$ and $\psi$ have Grassmann parity $0$ and ghost number $0$; $c_{\mathrm{gh}}$ has parity $1$ and ghost number $1$; $\bar c$ has parity $1$ and ghost number $-1$; and $B$ has parity $0$ and ghost number $0$. The ghost and nonminimal variables are formal algebraic generators; no state-space or positivity claim is made. The generators $c_{\mathrm{gh}},\bar c,B$ carry no physical unit assignment, and the differential below is dimensionless. The subscript distinguishes the ghost from the speed of light $c_{\mathrm{light}}$.

Let $s$ vanish on the coefficient algebra, so $s f=0$ for every $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb C)$. Thus $s$ is $C^\infty(\mathbb M;\mathbb C)$-linear.

Define the odd derivation $s:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P$ of ghost number $1$ by
$$
sa_\mu=\partial_\mu c_{\mathrm{gh}},\qquad sc_{\mathrm{gh}}=0,\qquad s\bar c=B,\qquad sB=0,\qquad s\psi=igc_{\mathrm{gh}}\psi .
$$
Extend $s$ by the graded Leibniz rule $s(XY)=(sX)Y+(-1)^{|X|}X(sY)$ for homogeneous $X$, where $|X|$ is Grassmann parity, and by $s(\partial^\beta X)=\partial^\beta(sX)$ for every multi-index $\beta$. This is an off-shell local algebraic differential for the Abelian gauge transformations; it is not a BRST charge on a Hilbert space and it does not assert existence of a gauge-invariant quantum theory.

items.title: Nilpotence and contraction of nonminimal doublets
items.statement:
The Abelian jet derivation $s$ defined in the local BRST algebra satisfies $s^2=0$. More generally, take any finite set of jet doublets $u^j,v^j$ with $|v^j|=|u^j|+1\pmod 2$, $\operatorname{gh}(v^j)=\operatorname{gh}(u^j)+1$, $su^j=v^j$, and $sv^j=0$, and suppose the transformations of all other generators are independent of these doublets. Define the doublet-number operator
$$N=\sum_j\left(u^j\frac{\partial_L}{\partial u^j}+v^j\frac{\partial_L}{\partial v^j}\right)$$
and the odd homotopy $h=\sum_j u^j\frac{\partial_L}{\partial v^j}$, using left graded derivatives. Then $[N,s]=0$ and $sh+hs=N$. Consequently the inclusion of the doublet-independent polynomial subalgebra induces an isomorphism on polynomial BRST cohomology. In particular, if $sa_k=0$ and $Na_k=ka_k$ for a positive integer $k$, then $a_k=s(ha_k/k)$.

For a ghost-number grading, write this cohomology as
$$H^r(s,\mathcal P)=\ker(s:\mathcal P^r\to\mathcal P^{r+1})/\operatorname{im}(s:\mathcal P^{r-1}\to\mathcal P^r).$$

items.title: Relative local BRST cohomology
items.statement:
Use the four-dimensional coordinate and jet algebra and nilpotent differential $s$ fixed by the earlier Abelian local BRST definition and nilpotence lemma. For integers $r$ and $0\le p\le4$, a compactly supported local horizontal $p$-form of ghost number $r$ is a finite sum of terms
$$f_{i_1\ldots i_p}(x,z)\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_p},$$
where each coefficient is smooth and compactly supported in $x\in\mathbb R^4$, polynomial in finitely many field-jet coordinates $z$, and homogeneous of ghost number $r$. Denote this space by $\Omega^{r,p}_{\mathrm{loc},c}$. A left derivative is used for odd jet coordinates.

For each spacetime index $\mu$, define the total derivative on a local coefficient by
$$D_\mu=\frac{\partial}{\partial x^\mu}+\sum_{i,\alpha}z^i_{\alpha+e_\mu}\frac{\partial_L}{\partial z^i_\alpha},$$
where $\alpha$ ranges over multi-indices, $i$ over the field and ghost generators, and $e_\mu$ is the multi-index with one derivative in direction $\mu$. The horizontal exterior derivative is $d_H=dx^\mu\wedge D_\mu$. It satisfies $d_H^2=0$. Extend $s$ to a homogeneous $p$-form by $s\omega=(-1)^p s_{\mathrm{coeff}}\omega$, where $s_{\mathrm{coeff}}$ acts on its coefficient by the earlier local BRST definition; then $s^2=0$ and $s d_H+d_Hs=0$.

Set $\Omega^{r,p}_{\mathrm{loc},c}=0$ for $p<0$ or $p>4$. Evaluation of a compactly supported local four-form on any smooth off-shell configuration is a finite integral.

For a graded subcomplex $\mathcal K^{r,p}\subseteq\Omega^{r,p}_{\mathrm{loc},c}$ stable under $s$ and $d_H$, define
$$Z^{r,p}(s|d_H;\mathcal K)=\{a_p\in\mathcal K^{r,p}:\ s a_p+d_Ha_{p-1}=0\text{ for some }a_{p-1}\in\mathcal K^{r+1,p-1}\}$$
and
$$B^{r,p}(s|d_H;\mathcal K)=\{s b_p+d_Hc_{p-1}:\ b_p\in\mathcal K^{r-1,p},\ c_{p-1}\in\mathcal K^{r,p-1}\}.$$
The relative local BRST cohomology is $H^{r,p}(s|d_H;\mathcal K)=Z^{r,p}/B^{r,p}$. In four dimensions, $H^1(s|d_H)$ is shorthand for $H^{1,4}(s|d_H)$. For compactly supported coefficients, $\int_{\mathbb R^4}d_Hc_3=0$ by the one-variable fundamental theorem of calculus in each coordinate and Fubini's theorem, so the quotient by $d_H$ identifies densities that define the same integrated local functional.

items.title: Wess–Zumino consistency is an obstruction class
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice, fix admissible flat scalar free data and a local scalar polynomial class under a scalar formal time-ordering theorem, and work conditionally in a time-ordering scheme satisfying that theorem's statement. At order $n$, let $\mathcal K_n$ be an $s,d_H$-stable subcomplex of the compactly supported local-form spaces defined earlier, with $\mathcal K_n^{0,4}$ exactly the allowed local counterterm densities. For each ghost number $r$, put
$$\mathscr F_n^r:=\mathcal K_n^{r,4}/d_H\mathcal K_n^{r,3},$$
the local-functional quotient formed using this same subcomplex, and let $\mathscr F_n^\bullet\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ denote formal power series. Let $\mathcal W_\hbar=s+\sum_{j\ge1}\hbar^j\mathcal W_j$ be an odd formal operator of ghost number one on this module, with $\mathcal W_\hbar^2=0$ and leading coefficient the induced $s$. Let $X\in\mathscr F_n^0\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$ and suppose its first possible breaking is
$$\mathcal W_\hbar X=\hbar^n\mathcal A+O(\hbar^{n+1}),\qquad n\ge1,\qquad \mathcal A=[a_4]_{\mathscr F_n},$$
where $\hbar$ is a formal indeterminate, $O(\hbar^{n+1})$ means terms of formal degree at least $n+1$, every lower coefficient vanishes, and $a_4\in\mathcal K_n^{1,4}$ is a compactly supported local four-form of ghost number one. Then $s a_4$ is $d_H$-exact within $\mathcal K_n$. There exists an admissible counterterm $b_4\in\mathcal K_n^{0,4}$ such that the shift $X\mapsto X-\hbar^n[b_4]_{\mathscr F_n}$ cancels the order-$n$ breaking in $\mathscr F_n^1$ if and only if
$$[a_4]_{s|d_H}=0\quad\text{in}\quad H^{1,4}(s|d_H;\mathcal K_n).$$
This is a conditional obstruction statement. Locality of $a_4$, nilpotence of the formal Ward differential, and admissibility of the counterterm space are assumptions; the result does not establish a quantum action principle.

title: Off-shell gauge complexes, BRST doublets and anomaly obstructions — Examples

items.title: Gauge-fixing doublets cannot create a new polynomial class
items.statement:
In the local Abelian BRST algebra, take the nonminimal pair $\bar c,B$ with $\bar c$ odd, ghost number $-1$, $B$ even, ghost number $0$, and $s\bar c=B$, $sB=0$. The polynomial $B^2$ is $s$-closed, has doublet degree two, and is exact:
$$B^2=s(\bar c B)=s\left(\frac{hB^2}{2}\right).$$
This finite polynomial calculation illustrates removal of a doublet class. It does not establish positivity of any physical Hilbert-space quotient.
